subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A two-year-old insists on doing simple tasks (like putting on shoes) by themselves, becoming upset when helped unnecessarily. In Erikson's terms, this reflects the crisis of:
explanation: The toddler stage (roughly 1-3 years) centres on developing autonomy through self-directed action; excessive criticism/over-control at this stage can foster shame and self-doubt instead.

stem: A four-year-old eagerly plans and initiates pretend games with peers, taking charge of the storyline. This reflects Erikson's stage of:
explanation: The preschool stage (roughly 3-6 years) centres on initiative — planning and leading activities; excessive restriction can instead foster guilt about self-initiated action.
